questions.stem:
A geometric series has first term $a = 360$ and common ratio $r = \frac{7}{8}$

Giving your answers to 3 significant figures where appropriate, find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the 20th term of the series,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Uses $360\times\left(\frac{7}{8}\right)^{19}$, to obtain 28.5
A1: Accept 28.47, or 28.474 or indeed 28.47446075
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (a) M1: Correct use of formula with power = 19
- Alternative to (a) Gives all 20 terms 315, 275.6(25), 241.17(1875), … (1st 3 accurate) M1. All correct and last term as above A1: Accept 28.5, 28.47, or 28.474 or indeed 28.47446075

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the sum of the first 20 terms of the series,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Uses $S = \frac{360(1-(\frac{7}{8})^{20})}{1-\frac{7}{8}}$, or $S = \frac{360((\frac{7}{8})^{20}-1)}{\frac{7}{8}-1}$ to obtain 2680
A1: Accept 2681, 2680.7, 2680.68 or 2680.679 or indeed 2680.678775 (N.B. 2680.67 or 2680.0 is A0)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (b) M1: Correct use of formula with $n$ = 20
- Alternative to (b) Gives all 20 terms 315, 275.6(25), 241.17(1875), … (1st 3 accurate) and adds M1. Sum correct A1: Accept 2680, 2681, 2680.7, 2680.68 or 2680.679 or indeed 2680.678775

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the sum to infinity of the series.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: Uses $S_\infty = \frac{360}{1-\frac{7}{8}}$, to obtain 2880
A1 cao: Accept 2880 only
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (c) M1: Correct use of formula

questions.stem:
A circle $C$ has centre $(-1, 7)$ and passes through the point $(0, 0)$. Find an equation for $C$.
(4)

parts.text:
A circle $C$ has centre $(-1, 7)$ and passes through the point $(0, 0)$. Find an equation for $C$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: The equation of the circle is $(x+1)^2+(y-7)^2=(r^2)$
A1: correct signs (just LHS)
M1: The radius of the circle is $\sqrt{(-1)^2+7^2}=\sqrt{50}$ or $5\sqrt{2}$ or $r^2=50$
A1: So $(x+1)^2+(y-7)^2=50$ or equivalent, cao for cartesian equation with numerical values but allow $(\sqrt{50})^2$ or $(5\sqrt{2})^2$ or any exact equivalent. A correct answer implies a correct method – so answer given with no working earns all four marks for this question.
Alternative method: M1: Equation of circle is $x^2+y^2\pm 2x\pm 14y+c=0$; A1: Equation of circle is $x^2+y^2+2x-14y+c=0$; M1: Uses $(0,0)$ to give $c=0$, or finds $r=\sqrt{(-1)^2+7^2}=\sqrt{50}$ or $5\sqrt{2}$ or $r^2=50$; A1: So $x^2+y^2+2x-14y=0$ or equivalent
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 is for this expression on left hand side– allow errors in sign of 1 and 7.
- M1 is for Pythagoras or substitution into equation of circle to give $r$ or $r^2$. Giving this value as diameter is M0

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the first 4 terms of the binomial expansion, in ascending powers of $x$, of
$\left(1+\frac{x}{4}\right)^8$
giving each term in its simplest form.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $(1+\frac{x}{4})^8 = 1+2x+..,$
M1 A1: $+\frac{8\times 7}{2}(\frac{x}{4})^2+\frac{8\times 7\times 6}{2\times 3}(\frac{x}{4})^3,$
A1: $=+\frac{7}{4}x^2+\frac{7}{8}x^3$ or $=+1.75x^2+0.875x^3$
(a) B1 must be simplified. The method mark (M1) is awarded for an attempt at Binomial to get the third and/or fourth term – need correct binomial coefficient combined with correct power of $x$. Ignore bracket errors or errors in powers of 4. Accept any notation for ${}^8C_2$ and ${}^8C_3$, e.g. $\binom{8}{2}$ and $\binom{8}{3}$ (unsimplified) or 28 and 56 from Pascal's triangle. (The terms may be listed without + signs). First A1 is for two completely correct unsimplified terms. A1 needs the fully simplified $\frac{7}{4}x^2$ and $\frac{7}{8}x^3$.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use your expansion to estimate the value of $(1.025)^8$, giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: States or implies that $x=0.1$
M1: Substitutes their value of $x$ (provided it is $<1$) into series obtained in (a)
i.e. $1+0.2+0.0175+0.000875$, $=1.2184$
A1 cao (3)
(b) B1 – states or uses $x=0.1$ or $\frac{x}{4}=\frac{1}{40}$. M1 for substituting their value of $x$ ($0<x<1$) into expansion (e.g. 0.1 (correct) or 0.01, 0.00625 or even 0.025 but not 1 nor 1.025 which would earn M0). A1 Should be answer printed cao (not answers which round to) and should follow correct work. Answer with no working at all is B0, M0, A0. States 0.1 then just writes down answer is B1 M0A0
Alternative for (b) Special case: Starts again and expands $(1+0.025)^8$ to $1+8\times 0.025+\frac{8\times 7}{2}(0.025)^2+\frac{8\times 7\times 6}{2\times 3}(0.025)^3,$ $=1.2184$ (Or $1+1/5+7/400+7/8000=1.2184$) B1,M1,A1

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) show that $\log_3 y = 1 + 2\log_3 x$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $\log_3 3x^2 = \log_3 3 + \log_3 x^2$ or $\log y - \log x^2 = \log 3$ or $\log y - \log 3 = \log x^2$
B1: $\log_3 x^2 = 2\log_3 x$
B1: Using $\log_3 3 = 1$
(a) B1 for correct use of addition rule (or correct use of subtraction rule). B1: replacing $\log x^2$ by $2\log x$ – not $\log 3x^2$ by $2\log 3x$ this is B0. These first two B marks are often earned in the first line of working. B1. for replacing $\log 3$ by 1 (or use of $3^1=3$). If candidate has been awarded 3 marks and their proof includes an error or omission of reference to $\log y$ withhold the last mark. So just B1 B1 B0. These marks must be awarded for work in part (a) only.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Hence, or otherwise, solve the equation
$1 + 2\log_3 x = \log_3(28x-9)$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:

M1 A1: Solves $3x^2 - 28x + 9 = 0$ to give $x = \frac{1}{3}$ or $x = 9$
(b) M1 for removing logs to get an equation in $x$ – statement in scheme is sufficient. This needs to be accurate without any errors seen in part (b). questions.stem:
$\mathrm{f}(x) = x^3 + ax^2 + bx + 3$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.

Given that when $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is divided by $(x+2)$ the remainder is 7,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) show that $2a - b = 6$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\mathrm{f}(-2) = -8+4a-2b+3 = 7$
A1: so $2a-b=6$ *
(a) M1: Attempts $\mathrm{f}(\pm 2) = 7$ or attempts long division as far as putting remainder equal to 7 (There may be sign slips). A1 is for correct equation with remainder $=7$ and for the printed answer with no errors and no wrong working between the two.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given also that when $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is divided by $(x-1)$ the remainder is 4,
(b) find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $\mathrm{f}(1) = 1+a+b+3 = 4$
M1 A1: Solve two linear equations to give $a=2$ and $b=-2$
(b) M1: Attempts $\mathrm{f}(\pm 1) = 4$ or attempts long division as far as putting remainder equal to 4. A1 is for correct equation with remainder $=4$ and powers calculated correctly. M1: Solving simultaneous equations (may be implied by correct answers). This mark may be awarded for attempts at elimination or substitution leading to values for both $a$ and $b$. Errors are penalised in the accuracy mark. A1 is cao for values of $a$ and $b$ and explicit values are needed. Special case: Misreads and puts remainder as 7 again in (b). This may earn M1A0M1A0 in part (b) and will result in a maximum mark of 4/6.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Long Divisions: $(x+2)$ into $x^3+ax^2+bx+3$ giving $x^2+(a-2)x+(b-2a+4)$ and reach their "3 - 2$b$ + 4$a$ - 8" = 7 M1. $(x-1)$ into $x^3+ax^2+bx+3$ giving $x^2+(a+1)x+(b+a+1)$ and reach their "3 + $b$ + $a$ + 1" = 4 M1. A marks as before

questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows the graph of the curve with equation
$y = \frac{16}{x^2} - \frac{x}{2} + 1, \quad x>0$

The finite region $R$, bounded by the lines $x=1$, the $x$-axis and the curve, is shown shaded in Figure 1. The curve crosses the $x$-axis at the point $(4, 0)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Complete the table with the values of $y$ corresponding to $x=2$ and $2.5$
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 1 & 1.5 & 2 & 2.5 & 3 & 3.5 & 4\\ \hline y & 16.5 & 7.361 & & & 1.278 & 0.556 & 0\\ \hline\end{array}$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1 for 4 or any correct equivalent e.g. 4.000
B1 for 2.31 or 2.310

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use the trapezium rule with all the values in the completed table to find an approximate value for the area of $R$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $\frac{1}{2}\times 0.5$, M1A1ft: $\{(16.5+0)+2(7.361+4+2.31+1.278+0.556)\}$
A1: $=11.88$ (or answers listed below in note)
(b) B1: Need 0.25 or $\frac{1}{2}$ of 0.5. M1: requires first bracket to contain first $y$ value plus last $y$ value (0 may be omitted or be at end) and second bracket to include no additional $y$ values from those in the scheme. They may however omit one value as a slip. N.B. Special Case - Bracketing mistake $\frac{1}{2}\times 0.5(16.5+0)+2(7.361+4+2.31+1.278+0.556)$ scores B1 M1 A0 A0 unless the final answer implies that the calculation has been done correctly (then full marks). A1ft: This should be correct but ft their 4 and 2.31. A1: Accept 11.8775 or 11.878 or 11.88 only. Alternative Method for (b): Separate trapezia may be used: B1 for 0.25, M1 for $\frac{1}{2}h(a+b)$ used 5 or 6 times (and A1ft all correct for their '4' and '2.31') final A1 for 11.88 etc. as before. In part (b) Need to use trapezium rule – answer only (with no working) is 0/4 - any doubts send to review.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Use integration to find the exact value for the area of $R$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1 A1: $\int_1^4 \frac{16}{x^2}-\frac{x}{2}+1\,dx = \left[-\frac{16}{x}-\frac{x^2}{4}+x\right]_1^4$
dM1: $=[-4-4+4]-[-16-\frac{1}{4}+1]$
A1: $=11\frac{1}{4}$ or equivalent
(c) M1 Attempt to integrate ie power increased by 1 or 1 becomes $x$, A1 two correct terms, next A1 all three correct unsimplified (ignore +c) (Allow $-16x^{-1}-0.25x^2+1x$ or equivalent). dM1 (This cannot be earned if previous M mark has not been awarded) Uses limits 4 and 1 in their integrated expression and subtracts (either way round). A1 11.25 or 11$\frac{1}{4}$ or 45/4 or equivalent (penalise negative final answer here).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- In part (c) need to see integration

questions.stem: Figure 2 shows $ABC$, a sector of a circle of radius 6 cm with centre $A$. Given that the size of angle $BAC$ is 0.95 radians, find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the length of the arc $BC$,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $r\theta = 6\times 0.95, = 5.7$ (cm)
(a) M1: Needs $\theta$ in radians for this formula. Could convert to degrees and use degrees formula. A1: Does not need units

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the area of the sector $ABC$.
(2)

questions.stem:
Figure 3 shows a flowerbed. Its shape is a quarter of a circle of radius $x$ metres with two equal rectangles attached to it along its radii. Each rectangle has length equal to $x$ metres and width equal to $y$ metres.

Given that the area of the flowerbed is $4$ m$^2$,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) show that
$y = \frac{16-\pi x^2}{8x}$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $kr^2+cxy=4$ or $kr^2+c[(x+y)^2-x^2-y^2]=4$
A1: $\frac{1}{4}\pi x^2+2xy=4$
B1 cso: $y=\frac{4-\frac{1}{4}\pi x^2}{2x}=\frac{16-\pi x^2}{8x}$ *
(a) M1: Putting sum of one or two $xy$ terms and one $kr^2$ term equal to 4 ($k$ and $c$ may be wrong). A1: For any correct form of this equation with $x$ for radius (may be unsimplified). B1: Making $y$ the subject of their formula to give this printed answer with no errors

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Hence show that the perimeter $P$ metres of the flowerbed is given by the equation
$P = \frac{8}{x}+2x$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $P=2x+cy+k\pi r$ where $c=2$ or 4 and $k=\frac{1}{4}$ or $\frac{1}{2}$
A1: $P=\frac{\pi x}{2}+2x+4\left(\frac{4-\frac{1}{4}\pi x^2}{2x}\right)$ or $P=\frac{\pi x}{2}+2x+4\left(\frac{16-\pi x^2}{8x}\right)$ o.e.
A1: $P=\frac{\pi x}{2}+2x+\frac{8}{x}-\frac{\pi x}{2}$ so $P=\frac{8}{x}+2x$ *
(b) M1: Uses Perimeter formula of the form $2x+cy+k\pi r$ where $c=2$ or 4 and $k=\frac{1}{4}$ or $\frac{1}{2}$. A1: Correct unsimplified formula with $y$ substituted as shown, i.e. $c=4, k=\frac{1}{2}, r=x$ and $y=\frac{16-\pi x^2}{8x}$ or $y=\left(\frac{4-\frac{1}{4}\pi x^2}{2x}\right)$. A1: obtains printed answer with at least one line of correct simplification or expansion before giving printed answer or stating result has been shown or equivalent

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Use calculus to find the minimum value of $P$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $\left(\frac{dP}{dx}\right)=-\frac{8}{x^2}+2$
M1: $-\frac{8}{x^2}+2=0 \Rightarrow x^2=..$
A1: and so $x=2$ o.e. (ignore extra answer $x=-2$)
B1: $P=4+4=8$ (m)
(c) M1: At least one power of $x$ decreased by 1 (Allow $2x$ becomes 2). A1: accept any equivalent correct answer. M1: Setting $\frac{dP}{dx}=0$ and finding a value for correct power of $x$ for candidate. A1: For $x=2$. (This mark may be given for equivalent and may be implied by correct $P$). B1: 8 (cao) N.B. This may be awarded if seen in part (d)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Find the width of each rectangle when the perimeter is a minimum. Give your answer to the nearest centimetre.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $y=\frac{4-\pi}{4}$, (and so width) $=21$ (cm)
(d) M1: Substitute $x$ value found in (c) into equation for $y$ from (a) (or substitute $x$ and $P$ into equation for $P$ from (b)) and evaluate (may see 0.2146 and correct answer implies M1 or need to see substitution if $x$ value was wrong.) A1 is for 21 or 21cm or 0.21m as this is to nearest cm

parts.label: i
parts.text:
(i) Find the solutions of the equation $\sin(3x-15^\circ)=\frac{1}{2}$, for which $0 \leqslant x \leqslant 180^\circ$
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $\sin(3x-15)=\frac{1}{2}$ so $3x-15=30$ ($\alpha$) and $x=15$
M1: Need $3x-15=180-\alpha$ or $3x-15=540-\alpha$
M1: Need $3x-15=180-\alpha$ and $3x-15=360+\alpha$ and $3x-15=540-\alpha$
A1: $x=55$ or $175$
A1: $x=55, 135, 175$
M1 Correct order of operation: inverse sine then linear algebra - not just $3x-15=30$ (slips in linear algebra lose Accuracy mark). A1 Obtains first solution 15. M1 Uses either $180-\alpha$ or $540-\alpha$. M1 uses all three $180-\alpha$ and $360+\alpha$ and $540-\alpha$. A1, for one further correct solution 55 or 175, (depends only on second M1). A1 – all 3 further correct solutions. If more than 4 solutions in range, lose last A1. Common slips: Just obtains 15 and 55, or 15 and 175 – usually M1A1M1M0A1A0. Just obtains 15 and 135 is usually M1A1M0M0A0A0 (It is easy to get this erroneously). Obtains 5, 45, 125 and 165 – usually M1A0M1M1A0A0. Obtains 25, 65, 145, (185) usually M1A0M1M1A0A0. Working in radians – lose last A1 earned for $\frac{\pi}{12}, \frac{11\pi}{36}, \frac{3\pi}{4}$ and $\frac{35\pi}{36}$ or numerical equivalents. Mixed radians and degrees is usually Method marks only. Methods involving no working should be sent to Review

parts.label: ii
parts.text:
(ii) Figure 4 shows part of the curve with equation
$y = \sin(ax-b)$, where $a>0$, $0<b<\pi$
The curve cuts the $x$-axis at the points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ as shown.
Given that the coordinates of $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are $\left(\frac{\pi}{10},0\right)$, $\left(\frac{3\pi}{5},0\right)$ and $\left(\frac{11\pi}{10},0\right)$ respectively, find the values of $a$ and $b$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: At least one of $\left(\frac{a\pi}{10}-b\right)=0$ (or $n\pi$), $\left(\frac{a3\pi}{5}-b\right)=\pi$ {or $(n+1)\pi$} or in degrees, or $\left(\frac{a11\pi}{10}-b\right)=2\pi$ {or $(n+2)\pi$}
M1: If two of above equations used eliminates $a$ or $b$ to find one or both of these or uses period property of curve to find $a$ or uses other valid method to find either $a$ or $b$ (May see $\frac{5\pi}{10}a=\pi$ so $a=$)
A1: Obtains $a=2$
A1: Obtains $b=\frac{\pi}{5}$ (must be in radians)
M1: Award for $\left(\frac{a\pi}{10}-b\right)=0$ or $\frac{a\pi}{10}=b$ BUT $\sin\left(\frac{a\pi}{10}-b\right)=0$ is M0
M1: As described above but solving $\left(\frac{a\pi}{10}-b\right)=0$ with $\left(\frac{a3\pi}{5}-b\right)=0$ is M0 (It gives $a=b=0$)
Special cases: Can obtain full marks here for both correct answers with no working M1M1A1A1. For $a=2$ only, with no working, award M0M1A1A0. For $b=\frac{\pi}{5}$ only no working M1M0A0A1
Alternative: Some use translations and stretches to give answers. If they achieve $a=2$ they earn second method and first accuracy. If they achieve correct value for $b$ they earn first method and second accuracy. Common error is $a=2$ and $b=\frac{\pi}{10}$. This is usually M0M1A1A0 unless they have stated $\left(\frac{a\pi}{10}-b\right)=0$ earlier in which case they earn first M1.
